fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides to help the first arriving unit identify it quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach both structures without repositioning.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive so responding units have an unobstructed path and clear sightlines to all structures.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the perimeter fence line to allow responders to move around the exterior of the structures on foot.
• Identify and mark any gate or opening in the perimeter fencing that provides the closest foot access to the rear of the property.
• Keep any perimeter fence gates unlocked or secured with a single breakable padlock so responders can reach the rear without delay.
• Post a simple property diagram near the front entry or driveway entrance showing the location of both detached structures and any rear access points.
• Establish a flat, open staging area near the driveway that remains clear of vehicles and equipment so arriving units have a consistent place to set up.
• Thin dense vegetation between the two detached structures to give responders a clear path between them.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Brush Area; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that overhang or touch any structure in the cluster.
• Thin trees within the tree cluster closest to the structures to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove brush from the brush area where it connects directly to vegetation near the structures.
• Clear dead material and loose debris from under large trees that stand close to any structure.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching any structure in the cluster.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees so vegetation does not form a connected path toward the structures.
• Keep the open green space free of accumulating dead grass, leaves, and woody debris.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches that could block a vehicle.
• Mark the primary access route so it is easy to identify from the road.
• Maintain the secondary access routes so they remain passable and free of encroaching vegetation.
• Cut back any shrubs or low branches along driveways that reduce visibility or narrow the travel lane.
